concepts.definition: Repeats a job a set number of times using a counter: it is made of a start, a condition and a step.
concepts.example: for (int pin = 10; pin <= 13; pin++) processes four pins in turn.
concepts.pitfall: Putting a ';' at the end of the for line: the loop body stays empty.

concepts.definition: The variable that keeps track of which round the loop is on. It is usually called i.
concepts.example: In the loop, i takes the values 0, 1, 2, 3 in turn.
concepts.pitfall: Changing the counter by mistake inside the loop.

concepts.definition: Stores many values of the same type under a single name.
concepts.example: int ledler[] = {13, 12, 11, 10}; holds four pin numbers.

concepts.definition: The position number of an element in the array. It starts from 0.
concepts.pitfall: Writing ledler[4] for a 4-element array: it goes past the end of the array.

concepts.definition: Adds 1 to the counter or takes 1 off it.
concepts.example: The loop for (int i = 2; i >= 1; i--) runs two rounds, with the values 2 and 1.
concepts.pitfall: Writing the condition the wrong way round in a counting-down loop (for example i <= 1).

concepts.definition: < means "if less than", <= means "if less than or equal to". It changes the number of rounds.
concepts.example: With i < 4, i = 0, 1, 2, 3 (4 rounds); with i <= 4, it runs 5 rounds.
concepts.pitfall: Using <= when walking through an array and going past its end in the last round.

quiz.prompt:
In this array, what value does ledler[2] have?

```
int ledler[] = {13, 12, 11, 10};
```
quiz.explanation: Indexes start from 0: ledler[0] = 13, ledler[1] = 12, ledler[2] = 11, ledler[3] = 10.
pin becomes 10, 11, 12 and 13 in turn. At 14 the condition (pin <= 13) is false and the loop ends. 4 rounds in total.
The last index of the array is 3. Because of i <= 4, the loop runs 5 rounds and reaches ledler[4] in the last round; that is outside the array. The correct version is i < 4 (or i <= 3).

quiz.prompt: In the "light that goes back and forth" program, 4 LEDs light up in turn for 200 ms on the way forward, and 2 LEDs on the way back. How many ms does one full round of loop take? (Ignore any waiting when the LEDs switch off.)
quiz.explanation: There are 4 + 2 = 6 lightings in total, and each lasts 200 ms: 6 × 200 = 1200 ms.
For i = 2 the condition (i >= 1) is true, so the body runs. It is also true for i = 1. When i becomes 0, the condition is false. 2 rounds in total.
